correctness.rationale: Rotation and reflection averaging preserve reproduction and contract the norm, leaving the two free real multipliers. The resulting normalized L¹ objective is convex, coercive by the Fourier coefficient bound, and differentiable since each nonzero kernel has only finitely many zeros. The mass and first cosine moment are both one, so the kernel cannot have constant sign. One sign change cannot make both sine moments zero. For two crossings, the second-harmonic equation forces the sum of angles to be π/2 or 3π/2 and their difference below π/2; then the third-harmonic equation cannot hold. The polynomial in cos(t) has degree at most three, so the three remaining crossings are simple. The stationary equations suffice by convexity. Equality in the midpoint L¹ inequality forces identical crossing locations and hence identical cubic up to scale, fixed by mass one. Integration on the four intervals gives the norm formula. For each real unital A, continuity and the substitution g=2f−1 identify its worst excess with (||A||−1)/2. For degree two, the a=1/2 kernel has one crossing at π/2 and vanishing derivative in the single free direction, establishing the stated 4/π benchmark. It is not stationary in both directions at degree three. Independent 80-digit replay gives 1.161395443269471428720196… and 0.080697721634735714360098…; maximum equation residual 3.17e−81 and separate interval quadrature agrees. The canonical delayed kernel has larger norm, about 1.18809092367265300728.
residual_risks: Uniqueness is for the even convolution kernel, not all real-linear operators. The proof's reference to three alternating sign intervals should read four intervals separated by three crossings; the formula uses all four. Numerical checks do not certify global optimality, which follows analytically.

value.rationale: This is a natural next transition band: once two freely adjustable multipliers are present, the optimum necessarily develops three crossings and cannot be inferred from the one-free-multiplier case. The exact kernel and its norm quantify the best achievable positivity tradeoff among all such reproducers and give a concrete replacement for the canonical nonminimal mean.
residual_risks: This is a fixed-band theorem, not a solution for all larger bands or a claim of positivity at the optimum.
